core_obligations: Reduce to a separated affine neighbourhood and write omega_X = f^!omega_S, identifying the object to be computed with i_x^!omega_X (proof lines 5816-5830).
Use finiteness of the residue field extension to factor i_x^! f^! = pi^! i_s^! and apply normalisation at s to get i_s^!omega_S = kappa(s)[0] (proof lines 5832-5848).
Compute Rpi_* of pi^!(kappa(s)[0]) and conclude that it is concentrated in degree 0 (proof lines 5850-5853).
proof_roadmap: Reduction and identification with a shriek (proof lines 5816-5830).
The finite residue field extension and normalisation (proof lines 5832-5848).
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian scheme S with dualizing complex omega_S, X of finite type over S with dualizing complex omega_X normalised relative to omega_S, and a closed point x of X lying over a closed point s of S, the lemma asserts that omega_{X,x} is a normalised dualizing complex over O_{X,x} provided omega_{S,s} is normalised over O_{S,s} (statement lines 5804-5814). After replacing X by an affine neighbourhood of x one may assume f : X -> S separated, so that omega_X = f^!omega_S (proof lines 5816-5822). The proof must show that RHom_{O_{X,x}}(kappa(x), omega_{X,x}) sits in degree 0; since the inclusion i_x : x -> X is a closed immersion, this complex represents i_x^!omega_X by Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-closed-immersion (proof lines 5824-5830). In the commutative square with i_s : s -> S and pi : x -> s, Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type shows that kappa(x)/kappa(s) is finite, hence pi is finite, and so i_x^! f^! omega_S = pi^! i_s^! omega_S; if omega_{S,s} is normalised then i_s^!omega_S = kappa(s)[0] by the same reasoning (proof lines 5832-5848). Finally Rpi_*(pi^!(kappa(s)[0])) = RSheafHom_{O_s}(Rpi_*(kappa(x)[0]), kappa(s)[0]) = the tilde of Hom_{kappa(s)}(kappa(x), kappa(s)), where the first equality is Example labelled example-iso-on-RSheafHom-noetherian applied with L = kappa(x)[0] and the second holds because pi_* is exact, so pi^!(kappa(s)[0]) is concentrated in degree 0 (proof lines 5850-5853). Recognising the localised complex as the shriek of the residue field and computing it through the finite residue field extension is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
